text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The funeral of nationalist leader Alpaslan Turkes on Tuesday is to be one of the biggest in Ankara in recent years.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan will meet Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in his two-day-long visit to Turkey. Erbakan delayed confirming the meeting.
- Erbakan orders a mixed gender choir not to sing the national anthem in his presence because females were part of the group.
- The interior ministry has sent a sent secret decree to provincial governors giving them a timeframe to implement an anti-Islamist purge demanded by the military.
- Coalition partners in debate on reshuffling the positions of 30 governors.
- The World Bank advices Turkey to sell public-owned enterprises to foreign investors under privatisation scheme.

- Turkey unsuccessful in registering informal "suitcase trading" by Russians and east Europeans because only a very limited number of shops have applied for a certificate to export goods since the beginning of March.
- President Suleyman Demirel vetoed a decree allowing Turks living abroad to become pensioners by paying the state in foreign currency.
